source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lebanon, Ohio campus publishes 35 MW of IT capacity, the largest published figure of any facility mapped in a state where only 9 of 79 sites publish a megawatt figure at all.

That gap is the real finding. Ohio has 79 mapped data centers and 9 published power figures summing to 118.4 MW, so this single campus is close to 30 percent of the state's known total. A state's data center footprint can look large by site count and remain almost entirely unmeasured by power, which is the number that determines how much compute can actually run.

The 35 MW is a power figure and nothing more specific. The operator publishes no rack count and no per-rack density, so any rack estimate depends on an assumed density rather than a disclosed one. The campus also publishes 400,000 square feet of technical space, which establishes room for a substantial compute footprint without establishing what is installed in it.

The certifications, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes, qualify the campus for regulated workloads including federal systems and health data. None names a tenant, and the spec publishes no tenants, pricing, or interconnection details. Whether AI workloads run here is not published, so the campus matters as a power asset in a state where published power is scarce, not as a confirmed AI site.
